events.reason: Both prior reports independently reached the same admission (accept), score_status (proposed), tier (5 assessed matching claimed 5) and near-identical gate reasoning for this single outcome family. The disagreement to resolve is a validation defect: one report's findings entries omitted the required evidence_refs field, failing schema validation. This corrected assessment restates the same substantive judgment (tier 5, all gates pass, no blocker) with evidence_refs populated for every finding, per the corrector's mandate to fix reported validation defects without altering the underlying merit judgment. The outcome is a usable provenance-preserving resource per the rubric's 'Source acquisition, rights resolution, digitization and preservation' row: it removes a material access obstacle (verified, agent-readable access to the full Beinecke scan set and additional RF1b-e/IT2a/LSI transliterations not previously catalogued), documents per-source rights, and supplies an inspectable acceptance test. It does not reach tier 10, which would require either independently authenticated execution of the verification pipeline (no context.execution_receipts entry exists) or demonstrated downstream analytical use/impact of this access route; neither is present in the supplied evidence. Overlap check: catalog entries are additive to the existing zl3b/gc2a/takahashi-original entries, so this is treated as a new family rather than requiring predecessor settlement.

This is an attributed external reference with disclosed provenance, not an unqualified redistribution claim of unverified bytes, consistent with the inclusion-first policy's treatment of applicable upstream open/public-domain bases.

Named human contributor (github_id 859355, gnuchev) with role attribution and full attribution share, plus explicit AI-use disclosure (Moonshot AI kimi-k3, tasks: download orchestration scripting, hash catalogue generation, doc drafting) with a stated human-verification step distinguishing AI-scripted tooling from the contributor's own fetch/verification.

Registers catalog entries (rf1be, it2a, lsi, artheon-lab-ms408) genuinely distinct from the zl3b/gc2a/takahashi-original entries already listed in research/context-index.json's source collection; this is additive incremental coverage, not a duplicate of the existing seed-corpus-parser or seed-source-catalog families.

No fabricated claim of independent verification beyond what is disclosed; the submission is explicit that hashes were computed from the contributor's own fetch, not an independently authenticated receipt, and the reference_only status of the Stolfi EVT is disclosed rather than concealed.
